thread:
jess: Hey — got an escalated customer (AcmeCorp) reporting ~600ms extra RTT + intermittent 503s. They are pinned to eu-west but traces show requests landing in us-east during a 12:15-12:22 window. Any idea?

ricardo: Ugh. Do we have an incident id / logs? Which API?

jess: Redwood text-generation API. Customer included a trace id: tx-0a9c5. They also attached billing screenshot — spike for cross-region egress.

ops-bot: alert: health-probe-eu-west instance-7 marked UNHEALTHY (probe_id=probe-3f, time=2026-03-15T12:16:03Z). fail_count=1, sample_latency=180ms, error="connection_reset_by_peer"

maya: That looks like a single-sample failure. Our failover policy has a 1-sample threshold for that pool for fast recovery. Could be a false negative.

support-l2: Customer says they saw a 503 and then a retry to us-east returned quickly — but they were billed for both. Is that expected?

infra-sre: Billing-wise retries are billed if they hit different model endpoints. We should check retry dedupe header. But first, reproduce the healthcheck flip.

samira: I pulled logs for tx-0a9c5: 
```
2026-03-15T12:15:59Z req tx-0a9c5 routed->eu-west:inst-7
2026-03-15T12:16:02Z healthprobe inst-7 result=FAIL reason=RST
2026-03-15T12:16:03Z routing reroute tx-0a9c5 -> us-east:inst-2 (fallback)
2026-03-15T12:16:04Z inst-2 processed tx-0a9c5 status=200 latency=45ms
```
So the probe fail and routing decision happened in-flight.

jess: So the healthcheck false negative caused an immediate fallback, which retried the same request. Customer sees double billing and higher latency from us-east.

ricardo: Do we need to change threshold back to 2 consecutive fails for that pool? What's the trade-off?

maya: That pool is tuned for low-latency failover for EU customers; raising threshold increases time to failover on real outages. But single-sample failures look noisy — likely transient network RST from host autoscaling.

infra-sre: Quick mitigation: disable cross-region fallback for this tenant (org: AcmeCorp) and force strictly-eu routing until we patch. I can push a tenant-routing override.

support-l2: Please confirm with customer before applying override? They asked for a fix ASAP.

samira: Repro steps we used locally:
1) curl -H "X-Debug-Trace: tx-test" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?region=eu-west
2) Drop single TCP packet from health probe source to worker (iptables -A INPUT -s <probe_ip> -m statistic --mode random --probability 0.01 -j DROP)
3) Observe probe fail and immediate reroute when threshold=1.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: routing-override for org AcmeCorp queued (change-id=chg-992) — requires infra-sre approval.

infra-sre: Approved. Applying override now.

infra-sre: Done. Verified tx-0a9c5-type test routing stays in eu-west even with single probe fail.

jess: I told the customer we applied a temporary override and that we're investigating a potential flapping healthcheck. They acknowledged.

maya: Root cause hypothesis: probe source network transient/RST from host scale-in combined with aggressive single-sample fail policy for that pool. Action items:
- increase fail_count threshold from 1->2 for eu-west general pool (prod change) — @infra-sre to schedule canary.
- add dedupe/at-most-once billing flag for cross-region retry billing (product + billing) — @support-l2 to open ticket.
- add additional logging around probe origin and instance scale events to correlate.

ricardo: For the postmortem: add timeline, customer impact (latency + billing), mitigation performed (tenant override), and follow-ups. Assigning postmortem to maya.

maya: Will draft. ETA EOD.

support-l2: Customer asked for a credit for duplicated charges. I'll coordinate with billing once we have the dedupe plan.

jess: Thanks everyone. If you find other tenants affected, ping this thread. :pray:

ricardo: FYI I scheduled a brief call with infra-sre for 15:00 to review threshold change risks.

samira: Added my repro script and logs to the internal ticket.

ops-bot: incident-note: temporary routing override applied for org AcmeCorp (chg-992).
